Courses.Title: Prin of Financial Accounting
Courses.Description: Designed for all business majors to introduce the core concepts of financial accounting and a complete overview of financial statement reporting.

Courses.Title: Prin of Managerial Accounting
Courses.Description: Designed for all business majors to introduce the core concepts of managerial accounting and a complete overview of managerial planning, budgeting, analysis and decision making.

Courses.Title: Intermediate Accounting I
Courses.Description: This is the first of a two-course series tailored for accounting and finance majors. It comprehensively explores Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and the reporting requirements established by the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB).

Courses.Title: Intermediate Accounting II
Courses.Description: This is the second course of a two-course series tailored for accounting and finance majors. It comprehensively explores Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and the reporting requirements established by the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB).

Courses.Title: Taxation I
Courses.Description: An in-depth examination of the taxation of individuals; an introduction to the basic concepts underlying the taxation system, including its structure and administration; and an introduction to basic tax research sources and techniques.

Courses.Title: Advanced Financial Accounting
Courses.Description: Understanding leases, pensions, and postretirement benefits, the equity method of accounting for investments, consolidation of financial statements, variable interest entities, partnerships, state and local governments, and not-for-profit entities.

Courses.Title: Auditing
Courses.Description: The capstone accounting course and the first of two courses designed for an in-depth examination of audit and assurance services for both public and private entities.

Courses.Title: Accounting Internship
Courses.Description: Designed for undergraduate accounting majors pursuing full-time, paid internships that are pre-approved and monitored by accounting faculty. A total of 75 work hours is required for each credit hour. Part-time internships must meet the same approval and monitoring requirements and will receive 1 or 2 credit hours depending upon the number of work hours required.

Courses.Title: Intro to Cultural Anthropology
Courses.Description: An introduction to the perspectives and methods of cultural anthropology. Topics covered include the nature of culture; the relation of culture to language; the importance of the environment for human societies; and a cross-cultural examination of family structure, social organization, political and economic systems, religion, and the impact of social and cultural change.

Courses.Title: Stories Across Cultures
Courses.Description: This course is an introduction to ethnography, which refers to both the process and end product of social science research that involves direct observation of, and interaction with, other humans. Described as both "art" and "science," ethnography aims to learn about and interpret culture and society. The result can be a book or journal article, or a visual production (ethnographic film). By reading ethnographic texts and watching films, we will learn how ethnographers have developed their research projects. We will also discuss ethical issues related to gathering data about humans, and our attempts to decipher meanings.

Courses.Title: Drawing I
Courses.Description: This foundational studio course offers an introduction to drawing concepts and techniques, with emphasis on line quality, value and placement. Various media such as pencil, charcoal, and pen and ink give students exposure to a range of materials.

Courses.Title: Two Dimensional Design
Courses.Description: This course focuses on the formal concerns of two-dimensional composition, including color, line, texture, repetition, and value.

Courses.Title: Digital Foundations
Courses.Description: Through this course students will explore a variety of ways to express visual ideas through digital media. Course topics cover digital processes with focus on the still and moving image. Assignments are designed to encourage creative and conceptual problem solving.

Courses.Title: Beginning Ceramics
Courses.Description: Beginning ceramics introduces the student to hand-built and wheel-thrown clay forms. Glazing and firing of finished pieces is required.

Courses.Title: Beginning Photography
Courses.Description: This course introduces students to photography as a fine art medium. Students will learn about design, exposure settings and creative camera controls while working on assignments focused on developing personal creativity. Enrolled students must have a DSLR camera.

Courses.Title: Painting I
Courses.Description: This course in an introduction to painting, exploring color, light, shape, and mass. The course covers basic materials and methods of paint application, as well as the preparation of supports and grounds.

Courses.Title: Figure Drawing I
Courses.Description: The basic proportions of the human figure, its skeletal and muscular anatomy, drawn from the live model form the basis of Figure Drawing I.

Courses.Title: Figure Drawing II
Courses.Description: The figure intersects with formal concerns of line, value, mark and placement in Figure Drawing II.

Courses.Title: Web Art
Courses.Description: Web Art focuses on creative applications of web design. Students learn how to create and optimize images for the web and the basics of HTML and CSS. The objective of the course is to develop personal work using computer-based art processes.

Courses.Title: Video Art
Courses.Description: Video Art explores the moving image as a means of creative, aesthetic, and critical expression. Through assignments based in video and audio production and editing, students will explore concepts related to time-based media and contemporary art practices while acquiring knowledge of camera functions, video editing software, and display formats. Art majors are encouraged to take Digital Foundations (ART 231) prior to Video Art.

Courses.Title: Special Topics in Art
Courses.Description: This designation applies to courses offered on an occasional basis in fields related to art.

Courses.Title: Painting III
Courses.Description: Painting III concentrates on advanced studio investigation of current ideas in painting. Exploration of contemporary and traditional procedures, materials, and issues in the context of a group discussion and review. Student produces a cohesive series of paintings as contracted by student and professor.

Courses.Title: Portfolio
Courses.Description: The Professional Practices class prepares art majors for careers and graduate study. Students organize their resume, portfolio, and senior thesis, while preparing for their senior exhibit. Emphasis is placed on learning to articulate concepts related to creative work and developing professional competencies. To be taken during the final year of study.

Courses.Title: Independent Study
Courses.Description: Guided study in an area of special interest under the direction of a faculty member.

Courses.Title: Internship
Courses.Description: Internships provide the student with an opportunity to apply classroom learning to the workplace and to explore potential career interests. This course may be repeated.

Courses.Title: Exploring Arts & Arts Admin
Courses.Description: This course is designed to expand students' awareness about the visual and performing arts and their function in our society. Through guest lectures, class discussions, and attendance at local arts events, students will investigate the role of arts in modern society. In addition, the course provides an examination of the field of arts management, offering students the opportunity to learn first-hand from local arts administrators about the systems that control the artistic process (including the management and organizational structure of arts institutions, marketing challenges facing the arts, and audience development and outreach.)

Courses.Title: Ballet I
Courses.Description: This course is designed for students entering Louisville Ballet's Studio Company, whether at Level 7 or 8. Registration is restricted to dancers admitted to the Studio Company through the audition process. Ballet technique classes are supplemented with a complementary curriculum including variations, pointe, pas de deux, conditioning classes, and additional instruction. Students are introduced to the culture and expectations of Louisville Ballet, and dancers will be called to exclusive studio company rehearsals along with rehearsals alongside the Professional Company, as well as with the Community Engagement team, to learn and rehearse choreography to be performed throughout the fall and spring semesters.

Courses.Title: Internship
Courses.Description: Internships are arranged with local arts organizations. Placement in local art, theatre, music and dance venues is based on the student's individual career objectives.

Courses.Title: Ballet V
Courses.Description: ART 460 is designed for third-year participants in the Louisville Ballet Studio Company and may include dancers at Levels 9 or 10. Students focus on the refinement of their technical skills, mastering more complex movements, with a growing emphasis on refining individual artistry and expression. Advanced students have enhanced opportunities to participate in Louisville Ballet Studio Company and Main Company productions.

Courses.Title: Ancient to Medieval
Courses.Description: A survey of painting, sculpture and architecture from a wide range of cultures. Beginning with the art associated with prehistoric cultures, the course continues through medieval Europe. The course is designed to familiarize students with key works of art and to promote an understanding of how they relate to their cultural context and fit into a historical evolution of style.
